<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a standard Arch Linux `.SRCINFO` metadata file, which is auto-generated from the `PKGBUILD` (via `makepkg --printsrcinfo`). It contains only package metadata and no executable logic, so it cannot itself run any commands, perform network requests, or manipulate files.

Analysis of the fields:
- **Source**: A single tarball fetched from the project's own GitHub repository (`https://github.com/mschabhuettl/bentwire/archive/v0.1.2/bentwire-0.1.2.tar.gz`). This is the expected upstream host for the package, pinned to a specific release tag (`v0.1.2`).
- **Checksum**: A real `sha256sums` value is present (not `SKIP`), which is good practice and pins the source integrity.
- **Dependencies**: `cargo`/`pkgconf` as makedepends and `alsa-lib`/`glibc`/`libgcc`/`libxkbcommon` as runtime deps are all consistent with a Rust (cargo) project building a Wayland desktop-character application. Nothing anomalous.

There is no obfuscation, no encoded blobs, no `eval`/`curl|bash`, no data exfiltration, and no unexpected network destinations. Everything is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard .SRCINFO metadata; pinned GitHub source with sha256; benign.</summary>
</security_assessment>

The build process uses standard Rust/Cargo commands (`cargo fetch --locked`, `cargo build --frozen`, `cargo test --frozen`) which respect the locked dependency tree. The package() function installs binaries, application data, a D-Bus service, a systemd user service, documentation, and license files to standard filesystem locations under $pkgdir. No obfuscated code, eval/base64 usage, network exfiltration, or unexpected system modifications are present. All operations are consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices and the application's stated purpose.</details>
